rules_applied: Whitespace removal (compact serialization)

Key sorting by UTF-16 code-unit value: 'C' (U+0043) < 'a' (U+0061) < 'b' (U+0062). JCS uses strict code-unit order, not locale-aware or case-insensitive sorting; uppercase ASCII letters precede lowercase.
Whitespace removal
Recursive key sorting: top-level has only 'outer'; nested object keys sorted as 'a' (U+0061) < 'z' (U+007A)
Array element ordering preserved (arrays are not reordered, only their object elements have keys sorted)
Inner object keys sorted: 'x' (U+0078) < 'y' (U+0079); single-key object '{"k":null}' unchanged
Whitespace removal
Key sorting: n1<n2<n3<n4<n5<n6 (already in order)
n1=1e21: IEEE 754 double value is 1×10^21 which is ≥1E+21, so ES6 ToString yields '1E+21' (exponential notation required for magnitude ≥10^21)
n2=1e-7: value is 1×10^-7, within [10^-6, 10^21), formatted as decimal '1E-7' — wait, 1e-7 = 0.0000001 which is <10^-6, so ES6 uses exponential: '1E-7'
n3=0.000001: value is 1×10^-6, exactly the boundary; ES6 formats values ≥10^-6 without exponent as '0.000001'

n4=100000000000000000000: this integer exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; nearest IEEE 754 double is 1×10^20, which is <10^21, but ES6 ToString for 1E+20 outputs '100000000000000000000'... actually 10^20 < 10^21 so it should be decimal. However the input literal 100000000000000000000 parses to exactly 1E+20 in IEEE 754. Since 10^20 < 10^21, ES6 outputs '100000000000000000000'. Correction: re-evaluating — 1E+20 is less than 1E+21 so ES6 does NOT use exponential. Output: '100000000000000000000'
n5=-0: IEEE 754 negative zero is serialized as '0' per ES6/JCS rules (sign of zero is discarded)

n6=333333333.33333329: parsed to nearest IEEE 754 double which is 333333333.3333333148...; ES6 shortest-representation yields '333333333.3333333' (trailing digits rounded to shortest unambiguous form)
Whitespace removal
Key sorting by UTF-16 code-unit value: '$'=U+0024, 'a'=U+0061, '€'=U+20AC, 'ü'=U+00FC
Sort order: U+0024 ($) < U+0061 (a, start of 'aa') < U+00FC (ü) < U+20AC (€)... correction: U+00FC=252 < U+20AC=8364, so ü < €
Final JCS key order: $, aa, ü, € based on first differing UTF-16 code unit: 0x0024 < 0x0061 < 0x00FC < 0x20AC
Whitespace removal
Key sorting: s1<s2<s3<s4<s5 (already in order)
String escape rules per RFC 8785/ES6: control characters U+0000-U+001F must use \uXXXX except for the allowed shorthand escapes \b \t \n \f \r and \\ and \"
s1: newline U+000A → \n (allowed shorthand)
s2: tab U+0009 → \t (allowed shorthand)
s3: double quote U+0022 → \" (required escape)
s4: 'é' is U+00E9, a non-control printable character, output as raw UTF-8 bytes (no escaping needed)
s5: trailing spaces U+0020 are printable, no escaping; if 'control' implied actual control chars they would need \uXXXX but as written with spaces they remain literal

weakest_point: Case 3, specifically the serialization of n4 (100000000000000000000) and n2 (1e-7). The rule in doubt is the exact ES6 Number.toString() boundary behavior: whether 1e-7 (which equals 10^-7, strictly less than 10^-6) triggers exponential notation '1E-7' vs decimal, and whether 10^20 (parsed from the 21-digit integer literal) stays in decimal form since it is < 10^21, or if precision loss during parsing causes an unexpected representation. I am least confident these two number strings are byte-exact against a reference JCS implementation.
